description: Deduplication window evicts newest messages (pop()) instead of oldest (pop(0)) when capacity is exceeded.
spec_notes: DedupWindow.is_duplicate_and_record must pop from index 0 on overflow.

repo_files.dedup_window.py:
"""Sliding deduplication window for streaming queues."""

class DedupWindow:
    def __init__(self, max_size: int = 5):
        self.max_size = max_size
        self.seen_ids = set()
        self.order = []

    def is_duplicate_and_record(self, msg_id: str) -> bool:
        if msg_id in self.seen_ids:
            return True
        self.seen_ids.add(msg_id)
        self.order.append(msg_id)
        if len(self.order) > self.max_size:
            # BUG: Pops from back self.order.pop() instead of self.order.pop(0)!
            # Evicting the NEWEST element instead of the OLDEST element!
            evicted = self.order.pop()
            self.seen_ids.discard(evicted)
        return False

tests.test_queue_dedup.py:
from message import QueueMessage
from broker import QueueBroker
from consumer import MessageConsumer


def test_basic_deduplication():
    broker = QueueBroker(dedup_size=3)
    assert broker.publish(QueueMessage("m1", "data", 1)) is True
    assert broker.publish(QueueMessage("m1", "data", 2)) is False  # duplicate
    assert broker.publish(QueueMessage("m2", "data", 3)) is True
    consumer = MessageConsumer(broker)
    assert consumer.drain_all() == ["m1", "m2"]


def test_fifo_window_eviction_order():
    broker = QueueBroker(dedup_size=2)
    # Push m1, m2 (window holds {m1, m2})
    broker.publish(QueueMessage("m1", "", 1))
    broker.publish(QueueMessage("m2", "", 2))
    # Push m3: window size 2 exceeded -> m1 (OLDEST) must be evicted, m2 & m3 kept
    broker.publish(QueueMessage("m3", "", 3))
    # Immediate re-send of m3 must be recognized as duplicate (m3 is in window)
    assert broker.publish(QueueMessage("m3", "", 4)) is False
    # m1 was evicted, so m1 can now enter again
    assert broker.publish(QueueMessage("m1", "", 5)) is True


def test_empty_broker_consume():
    broker = QueueBroker()
    assert broker.consume() is None


def test_sequential_unique_messages():
    broker = QueueBroker(dedup_size=5)
    for i in range(5):
        assert broker.publish(QueueMessage(f"id_{i}", "", i)) is True
    consumer = MessageConsumer(broker)
    assert len(consumer.drain_all()) == 5
